title: Ghost
tagline: Hands on the clay. Hands off the dessert.
about: A murdered banker's ghost tries to protect his girlfriend with the help of a fake psychic.
cue: Serve dessert when the pottery wheel scene starts.
faces: A NOTE FROM ODA MAE BROWN
"Hush, honey, the dead are talking, but I'm eating first. Tell Sam to wait his turn."
Luncheon from noon. Afternoon tea 3 till 5.
The lights dim at closing. Do keep together.
Crisp cornmeal fritters with spring onion and honey butter.
Garlic-rubbed toasts with ripe tomato and basil.
Rigatoni with sausage, fennel, white wine and cream.
Her sisters crowded round the table.
Rustic hand-folded apple galette with cinnamon sugar.
Pinot noir warmed gently with orange, cinnamon, star anise and a little honey.
THE BELL FOR THE PICTURE Serve dessert when the pottery wheel scene starts.
Prices include tea for one. Form TR-90. Images: TMDB

    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersHush puppiesCrisp cornmeal fritters with spring onion and honey butter.How to make it150g cornmeal75g plain flour2 tsp baking powder1 tsp caster sugar1 tsp fine salt200ml buttermilk1 egg3 spring onions60g butter, softened2 tbsp honey1 L vegetable oil, for fryingMix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a bowl.Stir in the buttermilk, egg and sliced spring onions to a thick batter.Beat the softened butter with the honey until smooth.Heat the oil to 180°C in a deep pan.Drop in teaspoons of batter and fry until golden, turning once. Drain on paper and serve hot with the honey butter.Tribeca loft crostiniGarlic-rubbed toasts with ripe tomato and basilHow to make it16 baguette slices (about 1 baguette)1 garlic clove4 ripe tomatoes1 small bunch basil2 tbsp extra virgin olive oilsalt, to tasteGrill the baguette slices until charred at the edges.Rub each warm toast with the cut garlic clove.Dice the tomatoes and dress with torn basil, salt and olive oil.Spoon the tomato onto the toasts just before serving so they stay crisp.MainsSam's Tribeca loft pastaRigatoni with sausage, fennel, white wine and creamHow to make it4 Italian sausages1 fennel bulb2 garlic cloves125ml white wine150ml thickened cream500g rigatoni60g parmesansalt, to tasteBoil the rigatoni in water with a good pinch of salt until just tender, then drain.Meanwhile, remove the sausage skins, crumble the meat and brown it in a large pan.Add the sliced fennel and crushed garlic and cook until soft.Pour in the wine and let it bubble down, then stir in the cream.Toss the rigatoni through the sauce with the grated parmesan.Oda Mae's pot roastHer sisters crowded round the tableHow to make itAs written, serves 4Beef chuck browned and braised at 160°C for 3 hours with onion, carrot, garlic and stock, potatoes for the last hour, gravy from the juices.SweetsPottery wheel pieRustic hand-folded apple galette with cinnamon sugarHow to make it1 sheet shortcrust pastry4 apples60g caster sugar1 tsp ground cinnamonHeat the oven to 200°C and line a tray with baking paper.Roll the pastry sheet into a rough circle on the tray.Toss the sliced apples with the sugar and cinnamon and pile in the middle.Fold the edges up by hand, pleating as you go.Bake until golden. Cool a little before slicing.DrinksMolly's studio mulled pinot noirPinot noir warmed gently with orange, cinnamon, star anise and a little honey, served steaming in mugs.How to make it750ml pinot noir2 strips of orange peel1 orange1 cinnamon stick2 star anises4 cloves3 tbsp honeyPour the pinot noir into a saucepan with the orange peel, the orange juice, cinnamon, star anise, cloves and honey.Warm over low heat without boiling, so the alcohol stays in.Strain into mugs and add a thin orange slice to each.
